case_studies.title: Beyond Leaderboards: A Method for Application-Specific Capability Profiling of Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Public leaderboards rank large language models (LLMs) in general, but an engineer has to choose a model for a specific application, architecture and cost. This paper presents a method for application-specific capability profiling of LLMs and its realization as a containerized testbed. The method treats each application as a unit of extension: an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration agent, a documentation-grounded chatbot or an enterprise-support automation agent runs in its own container behind a small contract, brings its own dataset, evaluator and owned attributes, and is onboarded together with i
case_studies.summary: This research offers a way to test and score large language models (LLMs) for a specific task, like a migration bot or chatbot, instead of just looking at general leaderboard scores. The authors built a containerised testbed where each application runs its own dataset, evaluation metrics and contract, giving a clear picture of how an LLM will perform and what cost it will incur. The result is a more accurate, cost‑aware model selection process that helps you pick the right LLM for a given workload.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure, here is what to do: 1. Deploy the authors’ containerised testbed in your environment. 2. Add your application’s dataset and evaluation scripts to the container. 3. Run the profiling to see which LLM meets your performance and cost targets before you spin up production instances.
